questions.q: What point from course 13 does this lesson reinforce about the CTA credential?
options: That it's a destination credential requiring substantial real-world implementation experience, assessed through a live design defense, not a next certification step
That it's a multiple-choice exam like the CSA, which anyone can schedule right after this course
That it requires no prior ServiceNow experience at all
That it has been discontinued by ServiceNow
questions.explain: The CTA sits at the top of the certification track as an advanced, experience-gated destination, not an incremental next exam.

questions.q: In the realistic multi-year trajectory this lesson walks through, what comes after an Administrator or Developer role and before CIS specialization?
options: Nothing — CIS specialization is the very first step
Immediately attempting the CTA design defense
A second Administrator certification
Several years of real implementation work across multiple projects, including exposure to architecture, integration, security, and governance decisions
questions.explain: The middle step — broad, real implementation exposure beyond narrow configuration — is what the lesson emphasizes as most often underestimated.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a CIS specialization is a real checkpoint, not just a resume line?
options: It is required before anyone can take the CSA exam
It's purely decorative and has no bearing on actual competence
It demonstrates genuine, end-to-end competence implementing a specific ServiceNow product area, signaling readiness beyond general platform familiarity
It automatically qualifies someone for CTA candidacy with no further experience needed
questions.explain: CIS credentials require demonstrating real implementation competence, marking a genuine step up from general familiarity with the platform.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why would someone with many years of narrow scripting work NOT necessarily be as CTA-ready as someone with fewer years but real exposure to architecture decisions?
options: Scripting experience disqualifies a candidate from ever pursuing CTA
CTA readiness is about having made real tradeoffs under real constraints across integration, security, and governance decisions — not simply time served
The CTA panel only evaluates candidates based on their total years of employment
Years of experience are the only factor that matters, regardless of what kind of work was done
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes time served from the specific kind of decision-making exposure the CTA panel is actually testing for.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say skipping straight from this course to a CTA attempt isn't a credible plan, and frames this as "by design"?
options: Because the CTA exam is purely random and unrelated to experience
Because ServiceNow made a mistake in how it structured the credential
Because this course path doesn't actually prepare anyone for ServiceNow work at all
Because the panel is specifically testing judgment built through real engagements, which can't be substituted by course completion alone — that's the credential's intended purpose, not a flaw
questions.explain: The credential is deliberately positioned to require real experience; that gatekeeping is intentional, not an unfair bar or an oversight.
